subject: Per-token rebate tranching & monthly burn-rate tranching plan for Q4 ramp
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@launchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rebate tranche idea + monthly burn tranching for your Q4 launch

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We talked through the broad commit you expect for launch (peak days + marketing-driven spikes) and you asked for a structure that protects Launchly from surprise overages in month 1 while letting you earn steeper per-token rebates as usage normalizes.

I sketched a practical approach and attached a simple workbook. High level:

- Monthly commit buckets (committed tokens per month) rather than a single annual commit.
- Tranches within each month that progressively unlock higher per-token rebate rates as burn crosses thresholds (e.g., 0–250M, 250–1B, 1B+).
- A 30% seasonal surge buffer for the first two months of the launch to absorb marketing spikes without immediate true-up.
- Mid-quarter true-up: if cumulative usage vs committed > 25%, we do a one-time true-up at a blended rebate instead of immediate invoice adjustment.

Questions for you:
1) Would you prefer the tranche thresholds set by absolute tokens or by percent of that month’s forecasted baseline?
2) Is a 30% surge buffer for the first two months defensible given your expected spend runway?
3) Any procurement constraints on monthly vs quarterly billing cadence?

Next steps I propose: my team (Marissa + Karthik) will turn this into a concrete table with example month-by-month dollar math. If that looks good we can seed the MSA and a DocuSign for approvals.

Attaching: commit workbook (editable) + placeholder MSA with an example clause for surge handling.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@launchly.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@launchly.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Rebate tranche idea + monthly burn tranching for your Q4 launch

Vanessa —

Appreciate the proposal and the workbook. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Tranches by absolute tokens make sense because our product team thinks in absolute call volumes for the new feature.
- The 30% surge buffer feels reasonable for month 0 (soft launch) and month 1, but we'd prefer month 2 to be 15% unless we hit explicit marketing milestones.
- Procurement prefers monthly invoicing with a single monthly true-up line item; they want to avoid multiple micro-invoices.

Also: is there a cap on the maximum rebate percentage (we need to show finance a ceiling for modeling)? And how do discounts stack if we pick a reserved capacity commitment in Dedicated later?

Elena
Sr. Director, Launch Experience
Launchly
elena.garcia@launchly.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@launchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rebate tranche idea + monthly burn tranching for your Q4 launch

Elena — thanks, this is helpful. Quick replies inline and then a proposal snapshot below.

- Tranches: absolute tokens per month — confirmed. We’ll show thresholds using tokens and % of month baseline for visibility.
- Surge buffer: agree to make month 0 and 1 at 30%, month 2 at 15% conditional on hitting the milestone you mentioned (marketing spend > $75k).
- Invoicing: monthly invoice with one-line true-up — doable.
- Rebate ceiling: we typically cap at 40% effective rebate vs public per-token list for hosted API; beyond that we discuss Reserved/Dedicated pricing.
- Stacking: Reserved/Dedicated discounts are handled as separate pricing lanes; we can show blended scenarios but the Reserved commit would supersede hosted per-token rebates for the committed capacity.

Proposed tranche table (example month):
- Bucket A (0–250M tokens): base price $0.00035/token, rebate 0% (effective $0.00035)
- Bucket B (250M–1B): base price $0.00035, rebate 12% (effective $0.000308)
- Bucket C (1B+): base price $0.00035, rebate 28% (effective $0.000252)

Surge handling: first two months — 30% buffer applied to committed bucket, usage within buffer billed at base price but not subject to penalty or immediate true-up; usage beyond buffer triggers monthly true-up at blended rate.

Mid-quarter true-up: if cumulative over-usage > 25% of cumulative committed for the quarter, we do a single blended true-up invoice in month-end close.

I’ve attached an updated workbook with the above numbers and three ramp scenarios (conservative / target / aggressive). Marissa and Karthik — can you review the workbook and confirm PS & onboarding SKUs for month 0?

Next actions for Launchly: review the workbook and confirm the marketing milestone condition (the $75k threshold). If OK, we’ll circulate a redline-friendly MSA with the surge clause and the monthly true-up language.

Thanks — Vanessa
